questions.text: Which accounting concept assumes that a business will continue operating for the foreseeable future?
questions.explanation: Going concern: financial statements are prepared assuming the business will keep operating. This justifies valuing assets at cost (not forced-sale value) and treating them as usable over future periods.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - mixed 12-Q test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: An expense incurred but not yet paid at year-end is called:
questions.explanation: Under the accrual basis, expenses are recognised when INCURRED, not when paid. An expense used up this year but unpaid at year-end is an accrual (a liability). A prepayment is the opposite: paid but relating to a future period.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - mixed 12-Q test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: The main purpose of a trial balance is to:
opts: Check the arithmetical agreement of ledger balances
questions.explanation: It lists every ledger balance so total debits can be checked against total credits - an arithmetic check of double-entry bookkeeping. It cannot detect complete omissions or wrong-account entries, and it never replaces the financial statements.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - mixed 12-Q test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which is an intangible asset?
questions.explanation: A patent has no physical substance but grants a legal right with future economic benefit - the Week 8 summary lists patents, trademarks, copyrights and goodwill as intangibles. Motor vehicles and furniture are tangible; inventory is a current asset.

questions.text: Insurance of N120,000 covers 12 months from 1 October; the accounting year ends 31 December. The year-end expense and prepayment are:
questions.explanation: Monthly cost is N10,000; October-December uses 3 months (N30,000 expense) and 9 months (N90,000) are prepaid.

questions.text: Using the same machine (cost N600,000, residual N60,000, straight-line over 6 years), its carrying amount after two full years is:
questions.explanation: Cost 600,000 minus two years of depreciation (2 x 90,000 = 180,000) gives N420,000.

questions.text: A business has assets of N850,000 and liabilities of N275,000. Equity is:

questions.text: Which of the following is an intangible asset?
questions.explanation: The Week 8 summary identifies patents, trademarks, copyrights and goodwill as intangibles.

questions.text: Amortisation is to intangible assets what ______ is to tangible assets.
questions.explanation: The guide pairs depreciation (tangible assets) with amortisation (intangible assets).

questions.text: A business with a year end of 30 September receives an invoice for rent of 6,000 covering the six months to 31 December. At year end the required adjustment is:
questions.explanation: October-December (3 months, 3,000) relates to the current period but is unpaid at 30 September, so it accrues.

questions.text: A business pays an electricity bill of 900 for the three months to November 2021; its year end is 30 September 2021. At year end:
questions.explanation: October and November (2 months, 600) are paid but relate to the next period, so 600 is prepaid.

questions.text: A prepayment adjusting entry requires a debit to:
questions.explanation: Debit the prepayment asset and credit the expense to move the unused portion out of the period's expense.

source.label: Double Entry Bookkeeping - Quiz 57: Accruals and Prepayments (answer marked on page)

questions.text: Beginning electricity accrual is 5,000, the ending accrual is 6,000, and 8,000 is paid during the year. The electricity expense for the year is:
questions.explanation: Expense = paid + closing accrual - opening accrual = 8,000 + 6,000 - 5,000 = 9,000.

questions.text: A prepayment is best described as:
opts: An expense for the current period not yet paid
An expense relating to a future period that has already been paid
questions.explanation: Prepaid expenses relate to a future accounting period but have already been paid; they are shown as a current asset.

source.label: Double Entry Bookkeeping - Quiz 57: Accruals and Prepayments (answer marked on page)

questions.text: Which equation correctly states the accounting equation as presented in the course material?
questions.explanation: The course pack states Assets = Capital + Liabilities: what the business owns is funded either by the owner (capital) or by outsiders (liabilities). B reverses the relationship, C is the profit formula, and D swaps the roles of assets and capital.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Essential formulas (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: A business has assets of ₦850,000 and liabilities of ₦275,000. What is its equity?
questions.explanation: Equity = Assets − Liabilities = ₦850,000 − ₦275,000 = ₦575,000, exactly as worked in the course's practice problem. ₦1,125,000 wrongly adds liabilities to assets; the other options ignore the equation entirely. Assets must equal liabilities plus equity.

source.label: ACC 101 worked practice problems — Problem 3 (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: Profit is best defined as:
questions.explanation: The course formula is Profit = Revenue − Expenses: profit is what remains of income after the costs of earning it. B would treat costs as adding to profit, C compares balance-sheet items, and D confuses expenses with the owner's withdrawals (drawings).

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Essential formulas (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: A machine costs ₦600,000 with a residual value of ₦60,000 and a useful life of six years. Annual straight-line depreciation is:
questions.explanation: Straight-line depreciation = (Cost − Residual value) ÷ Useful life = (₦600,000 − ₦60,000) ÷ 6 = ₦90,000 per year, as worked in the course problem. ₦100,000 forgets the residual value; the others misuse the formula.

source.label: ACC 101 worked practice problems — Problem 2 (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: Using straight-line depreciation of ₦90,000 per year on a machine costing ₦600,000, its carrying amount after two full years (no impairment or disposal) is:
questions.explanation: Carrying amount = cost − accumulated depreciation = ₦600,000 − (2 × ₦90,000) = ₦420,000, matching the course's worked answer. ₦510,000 deducts only one year; ₦330,000 deducts three years; ₦600,000 ignores depreciation.

source.label: ACC 101 worked practice problems — Problem 2 (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: In the straight-line formula (Cost − Residual value) ÷ Useful life, the residual value represents:
opts: The estimated amount the asset can be sold for at the end of its useful life
The total amount charged as depreciation over the asset's life
The cost of maintaining the asset each year
questions.explanation: Residual (salvage) value is the estimated disposal value at the end of the asset's useful life; only the portion of cost above it is depreciated. Deducting it spreads the depreciable amount, not the whole cost, over the life.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Essential formulas (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: An expense that has been incurred during the period but not yet paid at year-end is called:
questions.explanation: The course defines an accrued expense as incurred but unpaid: it must be added to the current period's expense because it belongs to that period. A prepayment is the opposite (paid in advance), a suspense item is a temporary holding for errors, and drawings are the owner's withdrawals.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Accruals and prepayments (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: Insurance of ₦120,000 covers 12 months from 1 October, and the accounting year ends on 31 December. The insurance expense for the year and the prepaid amount are:
questions.explanation: Monthly cost is ₦120,000 ÷ 12 = ₦10,000. October–December is 3 months, so the year's expense is 3 × ₦10,000 = ₦30,000, and the 9 unused months (January–September) are prepaid ₦90,000 — exactly the course's worked answer. ₦90,000 expense swaps the two figures.

source.label: ACC 101 worked practice problems — Problem 1 (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: The double-entry rule as stated in the course material is that:
opts: Every transaction has equal debit and credit entries, and whether a debit or credit increases an account depends on the account type
Debits always increase an account and credits always decrease it
Every transaction is recorded only once in the ledger
Credits are used for assets and debits for liabilities
questions.explanation: The course states every transaction has equal debit and credit entries, and warns that debits do not automatically mean an increase and credits do not automatically mean a decrease — the effect depends on the account type (debits increase assets and expenses; credits increase liabilities, capital and income). B is the classic misconception the course explicitly corrects.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Double-entry rule (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: A business buys office equipment of ₦250,000 on credit from a supplier. The correct double entry is:
opts: Debit office equipment; credit the supplier (payable)
Debit the supplier (payable); credit office equipment
questions.explanation: The business acquires an asset (debit office equipment, an increase in an asset) and incurs a liability to the supplier (credit payables). B reverses the entries; C wrongly credits sales, since no sale occurred; D wrongly debits cash when nothing was paid.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Double entry, ledgers and trial balance (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: A trial balance that fails to agree indicates:
opts: There may be an arithmetical error, though some errors (like complete omission) do not affect the trial balance
The business must have made a loss
The financial statements can no longer be prepared
All ledger accounts are automatically wrong
questions.explanation: The trial balance checks the arithmetical agreement of ledger balances; a disagreement signals an arithmetical error. However, the course's 'errors and suspense accounts' priority teaches that some errors — complete omission, commission, principle, compensating, reversal, original-entry — do not disturb the agreement, so agreement is not proof of correctness.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Errors, suspense and control accounts (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: A suspense account is used when:
opts: The trial balance does not agree and the difference is temporarily held while errors are located
Summarising cash sales at the end of each day
questions.explanation: Per the course's revision priorities on errors, suspense and control accounts: when the trial balance disagrees, the difference is placed in a suspense account until the errors are found and corrected with journal entries. It is a temporary device, not a normal classification account.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Errors, suspense and control accounts (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: Which of the following is capital expenditure?
opts: Buying a delivery van for the business
Buying fuel for the delivery van
Paying monthly rent on the shop
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure buys long-term assets used in the business (a delivery van provides benefit over several years and appears on the statement of financial position). Wages, fuel and rent are day-to-day running costs — revenue expenditure, charged to the statement of profit or loss.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Capital/revenue expenditure and adjustments (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: Treating revenue expenditure as capital expenditure in the accounts will:
opts: Have no effect on either profit or assets
questions.explanation: If a running cost is wrongly capitalised, it is not charged against revenue in the period, so profit is overstated; the amount also sits in an asset on the statement of financial position instead of reducing the asset's value, so assets are overstated. This classification error is one of the adjustments the course's 'capital/revenue expenditure' priority targets.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Capital/revenue expenditure and adjustments (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: Which document is issued by a seller to a buyer, showing goods supplied, quantities, prices and the total amount due?
questions.explanation: An invoice is the seller's request for payment listing goods supplied, quantities, prices and total due; it is the source document for recording a credit sale (and the buyer's purchase). Cheque counterfoils, bank statements and payroll records support cash and payroll records, not the sale itself.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Accounting concepts and source documents (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: The concept that income and costs are matched in the same accounting period as earned/incurred is known as:
questions.explanation: The matching (accruals) concept ties revenue and the expenses that generated it to the same period — it underlies accrual and prepayment adjustments, which the course lists as a high-priority topic. Money measurement records only measurable items, the entity concept separates business from owner, and consistency keeps methods unchanged between periods.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Accounting concepts and source documents (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: Under the entity concept, the owner's private car used strictly for personal purposes is:
opts: Not recorded in the business's books
Recorded as a business asset at market value
Recorded as a liability of the business
Recorded as a business expense every year
questions.explanation: The entity concept treats the business as separate from its owner, so purely personal items stay out of the business's books. Only when the owner injects or withdraws resources does it appear, as capital or drawings. Recording the personal car as a business asset, liability or expense would blur the boundary the concept forbids.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Accounting concepts and source documents (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: Cheques issued by the business but not yet presented to the bank appear:
opts: In the cash book but not on the bank statement
On the bank statement but not in the cash book
In neither the cash book nor the bank statement
In both, at the same value
questions.explanation: An unpresented cheque has been recorded in the business's cash book when written, but the bank has not yet paid it, so it is absent from the bank statement — the classic reconciling item the course's bank-reconciliation priority covers. Adjustments for it update the bank statement balance toward the true (adjusted) balance.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Bank reconciliation (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: Bank charges appearing only on the bank statement require the business to:
opts: Debit them in its cash book (reducing the cash balance) before reconciling
Ignore them until the bank sends an invoice
Add them to the cash book balance as income
Record them as a liability owed by the bank
questions.explanation: Bank charges reduce the business's true cash balance, and because they appear first on the bank statement, the business must enter them in its cash book (debit bank charges, credit cash) as part of adjusting the cash book before reconciling. Ignoring or adding them back misstates the balance.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Bank reconciliation (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: The statement of profit or loss shows:
opts: Revenue, expenses and the resulting profit or loss for a period
Assets, liabilities and equity at a point in time
Only cash received and paid during the period
The owner's drawings for the period only
questions.explanation: The statement of profit or loss measures performance over a period: revenue minus expenses gives profit or loss (the course's profit formula). Assets, liabilities and equity at a date belong to the statement of financial position; cash movements belong to a cash/bank analysis.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Final accounts (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: The statement of financial position presents:
opts: Assets, liabilities and equity as at a specific date
Sales and purchases for the year
Depreciation charged for the year only
questions.explanation: The statement of financial position is a snapshot at a date: what the business owns (assets), owes (liabilities) and the owner's stake (equity), with assets equal to liabilities plus capital. Flow measures like sales, cash paid or depreciation for the year belong in the profit-or-loss statement and its supporting workings.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Final accounts (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: A control account for receivables is used mainly to:
opts: Check the accuracy of the individual customer (sales ledger) accounts in total
Record the credit purchases of the business
questions.explanation: Per the course's errors, suspense and control accounts priority: a receivables (sales ledger) control account summarises the individual customer accounts, so its balance can be compared with the total of the personal accounts to locate errors. Credit purchases belong to payables records, and depreciation is unrelated to customers' balances.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Errors, suspense and control accounts (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: The main purpose of charging depreciation is to:
opts: Spread the cost of a long-term asset over its useful life as it is used up
Set aside cash in a bank account for replacing the asset
Show the asset at its current market value every year
Reduce the amount of tax the business pays by a fixed rate
questions.explanation: Depreciation allocates the asset's depreciable cost (cost minus residual value) over the periods that benefit from its use, matching cost to revenue. It is a bookkeeping allocation, not a cash transfer (B), a market revaluation (C) or a tax mechanism (D).

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Depreciation/essential formulas (MIVA practice questions.pdf)

questions.text: When goods are sold on credit, which ledger records the customer's personal account?
opts: The nominal ledger only, with no customer account
questions.explanation: Credit sales create personal accounts for customers kept in the sales (receivables) ledger, debited when sales are made and credited when they pay. The purchases ledger holds suppliers; the cash book records cash movements; the customer's account must exist, so D is wrong.

source.label: ACC 101 Full Exam Revision Pack — Double entry, ledgers and trial balance (MIVA practice questions.pdf)
